subject: Cognitive Science
title: Perceptual Constancy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Perceptual Constancy.

hook.text: A friend walks away from you. Their image on your retina shrinks—but you don't think they're getting smaller.

buildup.text: Size constancy is one of several perceptual constancies. Your brain maintains stable percepts despite changing inputs.

discovery.text: Color constancy does the same: a white shirt looks white whether you're indoors or in sunlight, despite huge wavelength shifts.

twist.text: The famous dress illusion ('blue/black vs white/gold') exploited a failure in color constancy under ambiguous lighting.

climax.text: Constancy mechanisms strip away the noise of changing conditions so you perceive a stable, usable world.

punchline.text: Your brain keeps the world stable—even when the signal doesn't.

quiz.question: What is perceptual constancy?
options: Perceiving stable properties despite changing input
